mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, مَا فِي السَّمَوَات وَالْأَرْض: i.e. "and what is in the earth" (وما في الأرض); then ما was omitted, on the basis that it is an indefinite described ما (nakira mawṣūfa) whose adjective, namely في الأرض, has taken its place. It is not good for ما to mean الذي and be omitted, because the ṣila (relative clause) does not take the place of the thing described according to the Basrans, while the adjective takes the place of the thing described according to all. So construing it according to consensus is better than construing it according to a disputed view.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t:
His saying الَّذِي لَهُ ملك السَّمَوَات: الذي is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it, or in the position of the accusative by [an implied] أعني ("I mean").
His saying وَهُوَ مَعكُمْ: معكم is accusative as an adverb, and the governing word in it is the meaning; its implied form is "and He is a witness with you" (وهو شاهد معكم).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying وَمَا لكم لَا تؤمنون: ما is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لكم the khabar (predicate), and لا تؤمنون a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying وكلا وعد الله: كلا is accusative by وعد. Whoever reads it in the nominative makes وعد an adjective of كل, so it does not govern it, and he puts it in the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "those — each Allah has promised the best" (أولئك كل وعد الله الحسنى). Some grammarians disallowed وعد being an adjective of كل, because it is definite, its implied form being كلهم; so the khabar (predicate) can only be وعد [with an omitted referring pronoun], and that is far-fetched, not permissible according to Sībawayh except in poetry.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying مَن ذَا الَّذِي يقْرض الله قرضا حسنا فيضاعفه لَهُ: its mention has preceded in [Sūrat] al-Baqara.
His saying قرضا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) that came not on the form of the maṣdar [of its verb], as He said أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا, and as they said أجابه جابة. It is also said that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as if He said "lends Allah lawful wealth" (يقرض الله مالا حلالا).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His saying يَوْم ترى: يوم is accusative, and the governing word in it is وله أجر. ويسعى is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because ترى is from seeing with the eye.
His saying بشراكم: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and جنات is its khabar (predicate); its implied form is "your good tidings are the entry into gardens" (بشراكم دخول جنات); then the muḍāf was omitted, and its meaning is that this will be said to them. Al-Farrāʾ permitted جنات in the accusative as a ḥāl, with اليوم the khabar of بشراكم; but جنات being a ḥāl has no sense, since there is no sense of a verb in it. He also permitted بشراكم to be in the position of the accusative in the sense of "they give them the good tidings", with جنات accusative by البشرى. All of it is far-fetched, because it separates between the ṣila (relative-like complement) and what it completes by اليوم.
His saying خَالِدين فِيهَا: accusative as a ḥāl of the كاف and the ميم.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t:
His saying يَوْم يَقُول: يوم is an adverb, and the governing word in it is ذلك هو الفوز; it is also said that it is a badal (substitute) of the first اليوم.
His saying فَضرب بَينهم بسور: the بـ is redundant (zāʾida), and سور is in the position of the nominative, an object whose agent is not named (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent). And the بـ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a striking with a wall" (ضربا بسور). [Translator's note: the two statements about the بـ are as in the source.]

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying وَمَا نزل من الْحق: ما means الذي and is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to ذكر; in نزل is the pronoun of the fāʿil (agent) referring back to ما. It is not permissible for ما with the verb to be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the verb would remain without an agent. Whoever reads نزّل with doubling puts in نزّل the name of Allah, exalted be His mention, as a latent pronoun, and assumes an omitted هاء referring back to ما, because when the verb was doubled it became transitive to an object.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t: His saying وَالشُّهَدَاء: nominative, conjoined to الصديقين, and لهم أجرهم ونورهم refers back to all of them. It is also said that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عند ربهم the khabar (predicate); and لهم أجرهم is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of الشهداء if you wish, the pronoun referring back to the martyrs only.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His saying اعلموا أَنما الْحَيَاة الدُّنْيَا: أنّ stands in place of the two objects of علم, and ما is the restraining ما (kāffa), because it restrains [أنّ] from governing; الحياة is a mubtadaʾ (subject), لعب the khabar (predicate), and الدنيا in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الحياة.
His saying كَمثل غيث: the كاف is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of تفاخر, or as a khabar after a khabar of الحياة.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying عرضهَا كعرض: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنة; likewise أعدت is also a naʿt of the Garden.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His saying مَا أصَاب من مُصِيبَة فِي الأَرْض: His saying في الأرض is in the position of the nominative as an adjective of المصيبة according to its position, because من is redundant (zāʾida); it may also be in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) according to the wording. In the adjective there is a pronoun referring back to the thing described. It is also possible that في الأرض is an adverb for أصاب or for المصيبة, and then there is no pronoun in it.
His saying تبرأها: the pronoun refers back to the affliction (المصيبة); it is also said: to the earth; and it is also said: to the souls. [Translator's note: «تبرأها» is as printed in the edition; the Quranic word is نبرأها.]

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying الَّذين يَبْخلُونَ: الذين is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), [or] as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) omitted, or in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of كل, or by [an implied] أعني ("I mean").
His saying فِيهِ بَأْس شَدِيد: a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحديد.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying أَلا ابْتِغَاء رضوَان الله: ابتغاء is an exception not of the same kind as the first (disconnected exception); it may also be a badal (substitute) of the accusative attached pronoun in كتبناها.
